source.text: וַיִּקָּבְצ֧וּ כָֽל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶל־דָּוִ֖יד חֶבְר֣וֹנָה לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֛ה עַצְמְךָ֥ וּֽבְשָׂרְךָ֖ אֲנָֽחְנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And gathered all Israel to David to Hebron, saying, Here, your bone and your flesh [are] we.

en.L: And all Israel gathered to David at Hebron, saying, "Look, we [are] your bone and your flesh.
en.B: Then all Israel gathered to David in Hebron. "Look," they told him, "we are your own bone and flesh.
en.R: Then all Israel came together to David at Hebron. They said, "We are your own relatives.

es.L: Y se reunió todo Israel con David en Hebrón, diciendo: «He aquí que nosotros [somos] tu hueso y tu carne.
es.B: Entonces todo Israel se reunió con David en Hebrón. «Mira», le dijeron, «somos tu propio hueso y tu propia carne.
es.R: Entonces todo Israel se juntó para ir a ver a David en Hebrón. Le dijeron: «Somos tus propios parientes.

fr.L: Et tout Israël se rassembla auprès de David à Hébron, en disant : « Voici, nous [sommes] tes os et ta chair.
fr.B: Alors tout Israël se rassembla auprès de David à Hébron. « Vois, lui dirent-ils, nous sommes de tes os et de ta chair.
fr.R: Alors tout Israël est venu se réunir auprès de David à Hébron. Ils lui ont dit : « Nous sommes de ta propre famille.

sw.L: Israeli wote wakakusanyika kwa Daudi huko Hebroni, wakisema, "Tazama, sisi [ni] mfupa wako na nyama yako.
sw.B: Kisha Israeli wote walikusanyika kwa Daudi huko Hebroni. Wakamwambia, "Tazama, sisi ni mfupa wako na nyama yako mwenyewe.
sw.R: Kisha Israeli wote walikusanyika kwa Daudi huko Hebroni. Wakasema, "Sisi ni ndugu zako wa damu.

vi.L: Tất cả Y-sơ-ra-ên tụ họp lại cùng Đa-vít tại Hếp-rôn mà nói: "Kìa, chúng tôi [là] xương thịt của ngài.
vi.B: Bấy giờ tất cả Y-sơ-ra-ên tụ họp lại cùng Đa-vít tại Hếp-rôn. Họ thưa: "Chúng tôi đây là cốt nhục của ngài.
vi.R: Rồi tất cả dân Y-sơ-ra-ên kéo đến gặp Đa-vít tại Hếp-rôn. Họ nói: "Chúng tôi là bà con ruột thịt của ngài.

ko.L: 그리고 온 이스라엘이 헤브론으로 다윗에게 모여 말했다. "보십시오, 우리는 당신의 뼈요 당신의 살[입니다].
ko.B: 그때 온 이스라엘이 헤브론으로 다윗에게 모여 와서 말했다. "보십시오, 우리는 당신과 한 뼈, 한 살입니다.
ko.R: 그때 온 이스라엘이 헤브론으로 다윗을 찾아와 모였다. 그들이 말했다. "우리는 당신의 친척입니다.

pt.L: E todo o Israel se reuniu a Davi em Hebrom, dizendo: "Eis que nós [somos] o seu osso e a sua carne.
pt.B: Então todo o Israel se reuniu com Davi em Hebrom. "Veja", disseram a ele, "nós somos do seu próprio osso e da sua própria carne.
pt.R: Então todo o Israel se reuniu com Davi em Hebrom. Eles disseram: "Nós somos parentes do senhor.

decisions.choice: 2 Samuel 5:1-3 is the source of verses 1-3: "all Israel gathered" in place of "all the tribes of Israel came"
decisions.reason: Chronicles retells 2 Samuel 5:1-3 almost word for word. Here it says "all Israel gathered to David" where Samuel has "all the tribes of Israel came to David", and "saying" where Samuel has "and said, saying". Chronicles moves straight from Saul's death (chapter 10) to this scene. It leaves out David's seven and a half years as king of Judah alone and the war with Saul's house (2 Samuel 2-4), so the whole nation is seen coming to David at once.

decisions.choice: your bone and your flesh: your own kin, people of the same family
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:1. To be someone's bone and flesh is to be closely related to him (Genesis 2:23; 29:14; Judges 9:2). The people remind David that they belong to the same nation, descended from the same ancestor, Israel.

decisions.choice: your own relatives
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of bone and flesh by its meaning, family kinship, as in 2 Samuel 5:1.

decisions.choice: Y se reunió todo Israel con David (L); se reunió (B); se juntó para ir a ver a David (R)
decisions.reason: Chronicles has "all Israel gathered" where 2 Samuel 5:1 has "all the tribes came"; the rest of the verse keeps the Spanish wording of 2 Samuel 5:1 at each level, changing only the verb and its subject.

decisions.choice: passé simple at L and B, passé composé at R; wording of 2 Samuel 5:1-3 reused
decisions.reason: For this block (1 Chronicles 11-29): narration is in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced and the passé composé at Readable, as the French style guide and the Kings terms note set. Where Chronicles retells Samuel with the same Hebrew, the French of 2 Samuel is kept and only what the Hebrew changes is changed: here "tout Israël se rassembla" for Samuel’s "toutes les tribus d’Israël vinrent".

decisions.choice: Israeli wote wakakusanyika (L) / walikusanyika (B, R)
decisions.reason: Chronicles has "all Israel gathered" where 2 Samuel 5:1 has "all the tribes of Israel came"; the Swahili of 2 Samuel 5:1 is kept and only these words change.

decisions.choice: The people say "ngài" to David and "chúng tôi" for themselves
decisions.reason: As the Vietnamese 2 Samuel 5:1-3, which this passage retells; the whole block reuses the Vietnamese Samuel wording where the Hebrew is the same.

decisions.choice: The people speak to David in the formal polite style (합쇼체) and call him "당신", as in 2 Samuel 5:1-3, whose Korean wording this passage reuses
decisions.reason: He is not yet their king when they come; Chronicles retells 2 Samuel 5:1-3 almost word for word, so the Korean keeps the Samuel wording and changes only "all the tribes of Israel came" to "all Israel gathered" ("온 이스라엘이 ... 모여").

decisions.choice: todo o Israel se reuniu; o seu osso e a sua carne (L, B); parentes do senhor (R); o senhor (the people to David)
decisions.reason: Verses 1-3 retell 2 Samuel 5:1-3 (m1), and the Portuguese of 2 Samuel is kept level by level, with "todo o Israel se reuniu" for Samuel's "todas as tribos de Israel vieram". As there, the people speak up to David as their king with "o senhor" and "seu", "sua".

source.text: גַּם־תְּמ֣וֹל גַּם־שִׁלְשׁ֗וֹם גַּ֚ם בִּהְי֣וֹת שָׁא֣וּל מֶ֔לֶךְ אַתָּ֛ה הַמּוֹצִ֥יא וְהַמֵּבִ֖יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּאמֶר֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ לְךָ֗ אַתָּ֨ה תִרְעֶ֤ה אֶת־עַמִּי֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאַתָּה֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה נָגִ֔יד עַ֖ל עַמִּ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Even yesterday, even three days ago, even when was Saul king, you [were] the [one] leading out and the [one] bringing in Israel; and said Yahweh your God to you, You will shepherd my people Israel, and you will be ruler over my people Israel.

en.L: Even yesterday and the day before, even when Saul was king, you were the one who led Israel out and brought [it] in. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God said to you, 'You will shepherd {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel, and you will be ruler over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.'"
en.B: In times past, even while Saul reigned, you were the one who led Israel out to battle and brought them back. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God said to you, 'You are the one who will shepherd {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel; you will become ruler over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.'"
en.R: Even when Saul was king, you were the one who led Israel's army out to fight and brought it home again. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God told you, 'You will be the shepherd of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel. You will be the leader of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.'"

es.L: Aun ayer y anteayer, aun cuando Saúl era rey, tú eras el que sacaba y metía a Israel. Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te dijo: “Tú pastorearás a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo Israel, y tú serás gobernante sobre {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo Israel”».
es.B: En tiempos pasados, aun cuando Saúl reinaba, tú eras quien sacaba a Israel a la batalla y lo traía de vuelta. Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te dijo: “Tú eres quien pastoreará a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo Israel; tú serás gobernante sobre {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo Israel”».
es.R: Aun cuando Saúl era rey, tú eras el que dirigía al ejército de Israel en la guerra y lo traía de regreso. Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te dijo: “Tú serás el pastor de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo Israel. Tú serás el líder de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo Israel”».

fr.L: Hier comme avant-hier, même quand Saül était roi, c’est toi qui faisais sortir et qui faisais rentrer Israël. Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’a dit : “C’est toi qui feras paître {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple Israël, et c’est toi qui seras chef sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple Israël.” »
fr.B: Autrefois déjà, même quand Saül régnait, c’est toi qui conduisais Israël au combat et qui le ramenais. Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’a dit : “C’est toi qui seras le berger de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple Israël ; tu deviendras chef de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple Israël.” »
fr.R: Même quand Saül était roi, c’est toi qui menais l’armée d’Israël au combat et qui la ramenais à la maison. Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu t’a dit : “Tu seras le berger de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple Israël. Tu seras le chef de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple Israël.” »

sw.L: Jana na juzi, hata Sauli alipokuwa mfalme, wewe ndiwe uliyekuwa ukiwaongoza Israeli kutoka na kuwaingiza. Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako akakuambia, 'Wewe utawachunga watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Israeli, nawe utakuwa kiongozi juu ya watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Israeli.'"
sw.B: Hapo zamani, hata Sauli alipokuwa akitawala, wewe ndiwe uliyewaongoza Israeli kwenda vitani na kuwarudisha. Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako alikuambia, 'Wewe ndiwe utakayewachunga watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Israeli; utakuwa kiongozi juu ya watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Israeli.'"
sw.R: Hata Sauli alipokuwa mfalme, wewe ndiwe uliyeliongoza jeshi la Israeli kwenda vitani na kulirudisha nyumbani. Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako alikuambia, 'Wewe utakuwa mchungaji wa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Israeli. Utakuwa kiongozi wa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Israeli.'"

vi.L: Cả hôm qua lẫn hôm trước, cả khi Sau-lơ làm vua, chính ngài là người dẫn Y-sơ-ra-ên ra đi và đưa [họ] về. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngài đã phán với ngài: 'Ngươi sẽ chăn dắt dân Y-sơ-ra-ên của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và ngươi sẽ làm người lãnh đạo dân Y-sơ-ra-ên của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.'"
vi.B: Trước đây, ngay khi Sau-lơ còn làm vua, chính ngài là người dẫn quân Y-sơ-ra-ên ra trận và đưa họ trở về. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngài đã phán với ngài: 'Chính con sẽ chăn dắt dân Y-sơ-ra-ên của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; con sẽ làm người lãnh đạo dân Y-sơ-ra-ên của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.'"
vi.R: Ngay khi Sau-lơ còn làm vua, chính ngài là người dẫn quân Y-sơ-ra-ên ra trận và đưa họ về nhà. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngài đã phán với ngài: 'Con sẽ là người chăn dắt dân Y-sơ-ra-ên của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Con sẽ là người lãnh đạo dân Y-sơ-ra-ên của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.'"

ko.L: 어제도 그제도, 사울이 왕으로 있을 때에도, 이스라엘을 이끌고 나갔다가 이끌고 들어오던 이는 당신이었습니다. 그리고 당신의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 당신에게 '너는 내 백성 이스라엘을 목자로서 돌볼 것이고, 너는 내 백성 이스라엘의 지도자가 될 것이다' 하고 말씀하셨습니다."
ko.B: 전에 사울이 다스리던 때에도, 이스라엘을 이끌고 싸우러 나갔다가 다시 데리고 돌아온 사람은 바로 당신이었습니다. 그리고 당신의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 당신에게 '네가 내 백성 이스라엘의 목자가 될 것이다. 네가 내 백성 이스라엘의 지도자가 될 것이다' 하고 말씀하셨습니다."
ko.R: 사울이 왕이었을 때에도 이스라엘 군대를 이끌고 싸우러 나갔다가 다시 데리고 돌아온 사람은 당신이었습니다. 그리고 당신의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 당신에게 '너는 내 백성 이스라엘의 목자가 될 것이다. 너는 내 백성 이스라엘의 지도자가 될 것이다' 하고 말씀하셨습니다."

pt.L: Tanto ontem como anteontem, mesmo quando Saul era rei, era o senhor quem fazia Israel sair e o fazia entrar. E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o seu Deus, lhe disse: 'Tu apascentarás o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo Israel, e tu serás príncipe sobre o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo Israel.'"
pt.B: Já no passado, mesmo quando Saul reinava, era o senhor quem conduzia Israel para a batalha e o trazia de volta. E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o seu Deus, lhe disse: 'Tu é que apascentarás o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo Israel; tu serás príncipe sobre o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo Israel.'"
pt.R: Mesmo quando Saul era rei, era o senhor quem levava o exército de Israel para a guerra e o trazia de volta para casa. E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o seu Deus, disse ao senhor: 'Tu serás o pastor do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo Israel. Tu serás o chefe do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo Israel.'"

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 5:2, with "Yahweh your God" and "ruler over my people Israel"
decisions.reason: The words follow 2 Samuel 5:2 with small differences: Chronicles has "even" three times; it says "when Saul was king" without "over us"; it calls God "Yahweh your God" where Samuel has "Yahweh"; and it has "ruler over my people Israel" where Samuel has "ruler over Israel", so the people are twice called God's own. Chronicles spells the words for "you were the one who led out and brought in" in the ordinary way, without the unusual spelling noted at 2 Samuel 5:2.

decisions.choice: yesterday and three days ago: in the past, for some time now
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:2. The pair of time words is a Hebrew way of saying "before now" (Genesis 31:2; Exodus 5:8). The people mean that David's leadership is nothing new.

decisions.choice: leading out and bringing in: leading the army to war and home again
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:2. To lead out and bring in is said of a commander who takes his men into battle and brings them back (Numbers 27:17; Joshua 14:11; 1 Samuel 18:13, 16).

decisions.choice: shepherd my people; ruler: the king cares for a people that belongs to God
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:2. The verb "shepherd" pictures a king who guards and feeds a flock that is not his own, and "ruler" is the word for a leader appointed by God (1 Samuel 9:16; 13:14). David was taken from the sheep (Psalm 78:70-72).

decisions.choice: out to battle and brought them back (Balanced); led Israel's army out to fight and brought it home again (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:2, Balanced and Readable say what the idiom of going out and coming in refers to, the leading of troops in war.

decisions.choice: leader
decisions.reason: Readable says "leader" for the word rendered "ruler", as in the rest of these books.

decisions.choice: tú, te (the elders to David)
decisions.reason: As in Samuel and Kings, one person is addressed with "tú", the king included; respect is carried by the words used, not by "usted".

decisions.choice: "지도자" for *nagid* at every level
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for *nagid*, and as 2 Samuel 5:2 has it.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 5:2: príncipe (L, B), chefe (R); tu (God to David); "o seu Deus" and "sobre o meu povo Israel" added
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:2 in Portuguese at each level ("príncipe" at Literal and Balanced, "chefe" at Readable, for the leader appointed by God; God's words to David with "tu"), changed only where Chronicles changes it (m1): "{{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o seu Deus", no "sobre nós" after "rei", and "o meu povo Israel" repeated in the second line.

source.text: וַ֠יָּבֹאוּ כָּל־זִקְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל אֶל־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ חֶבְר֔וֹנָה וַיִּכְרֹת֩ לָהֶ֨ם דָּוִ֥יד בְּרִ֛ית בְּחֶבְר֖וֹן לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּמְשְׁח֨וּ אֶת־דָּוִ֤יד לְמֶ֨לֶךְ֙ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד־שְׁמוּאֵֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And came all [the] elders of Israel to the king to Hebron, and cut for them David a covenant in Hebron before Yahweh; and they anointed David for king over Israel, according to [the] word of Yahweh by [the] hand of Samuel.

en.L: And all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and David made a covenant with them at Hebron before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and they anointed David [as] king over Israel, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by the hand of Samuel.
en.B: When all the elders of Israel had come to the king in Hebron, David made a covenant with them there in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they anointed David king over Israel, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had promised through Samuel.
en.R: All the leaders of Israel came to King David at Hebron. There David made a covenant with them in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they poured oil on his head to make him king over Israel. This was what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said through Samuel.

es.L: Y vinieron todos los ancianos de Israel al rey en Hebrón, y David hizo pacto con ellos en Hebrón delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}; y ungieron a David [como] rey sobre Israel, conforme a la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} por mano de Samuel.
es.B: Cuando todos los ancianos de Israel llegaron ante el rey en Hebrón, David hizo un pacto con ellos allí, en presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y ungieron a David como rey sobre Israel, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo había prometido por medio de Samuel.
es.R: Todos los líderes de Israel vinieron a ver al rey David en Hebrón. Allí David hizo un pacto con ellos delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y ellos le derramaron aceite sobre la cabeza para hacerlo rey de Israel. Esto era lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había dicho por medio de Samuel.

fr.L: Et tous les anciens d’Israël vinrent auprès du roi à Hébron, et David conclut avec eux une alliance à Hébron devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; et ils oignirent David [comme] roi sur Israël, selon la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} par la main de Samuel.
fr.B: Quand tous les anciens d’Israël furent venus auprès du roi à Hébron, David conclut avec eux une alliance en ce lieu, en présence {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et ils oignirent David comme roi sur Israël, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait promis par Samuel.
fr.R: Tous les chefs d’Israël sont venus voir le roi David à Hébron. Là, David a fait une alliance avec eux devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et ils lui ont versé de l’huile sur la tête pour faire de lui le roi d’Israël. C’était ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait dit par Samuel.

sw.L: Wazee wote wa Israeli wakaja kwa mfalme huko Hebroni, naye Daudi akafanya agano nao huko Hebroni mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; wakampaka Daudi mafuta [awe] mfalme juu ya Israeli, sawasawa na neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa mkono wa Samweli.
sw.B: Wazee wote wa Israeli walipokuwa wamefika kwa mfalme huko Hebroni, Daudi alifanya agano nao huko mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nao wakampaka Daudi mafuta awe mfalme juu ya Israeli, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyoahidi kupitia Samweli.
sw.R: Viongozi wote wa Israeli walikuja kwa mfalme Daudi huko Hebroni. Huko Daudi akafanya agano nao mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nao wakamimina mafuta juu ya kichwa chake ili awe mfalme juu ya Israeli. Ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa amesema kupitia Samweli.

vi.L: Tất cả các trưởng lão Y-sơ-ra-ên đến cùng vua tại Hếp-rôn, và Đa-vít lập giao ước với họ tại Hếp-rôn trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}; rồi họ xức dầu cho Đa-vít làm vua trên Y-sơ-ra-ên, theo lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} qua tay Sa-mu-ên.
vi.B: Khi tất cả các trưởng lão Y-sơ-ra-ên đến gặp vua tại Hếp-rôn, Đa-vít lập giao ước với họ tại đó trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và họ xức dầu cho Đa-vít làm vua Y-sơ-ra-ên, đúng như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã hứa qua Sa-mu-ên.
vi.R: Tất cả các trưởng lão Y-sơ-ra-ên đến gặp vua Đa-vít tại Hếp-rôn. Tại đó Đa-vít lập giao ước với họ trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và họ đổ dầu trên đầu ông để lập ông làm vua Y-sơ-ra-ên. Việc này đúng như lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán qua Sa-mu-ên.

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘의 모든 장로가 헤브론으로 왕에게 왔고, 다윗이 헤브론에서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 그들과 언약을 맺었다. 그리고 그들이 사무엘의 손을 통한 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀대로 다윗에게 기름을 부어 이스라엘의 왕으로 세웠다.
ko.B: 이스라엘의 모든 장로가 헤브론으로 왕을 찾아오자, 다윗은 거기에서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 그들과 언약을 맺었다. 그리고 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 사무엘을 통해 약속하신 대로 다윗에게 기름을 부어 이스라엘의 왕으로 세웠다.
ko.R: 이스라엘의 모든 지도자가 헤브론으로 다윗 왕을 찾아왔다. 다윗은 거기에서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 그들과 언약을 맺었다. 그리고 그들은 다윗의 머리에 기름을 부어 그를 이스라엘의 왕으로 세웠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 사무엘을 통해 말씀하신 그대로였다.

pt.L: E todos os anciãos de Israel vieram ao rei em Hebrom, e Davi fez com eles uma aliança em Hebrom diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}; e ungiram Davi [como] rei sobre Israel, conforme a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} pela mão de Samuel.
pt.B: Quando todos os anciãos de Israel vieram ao rei em Hebrom, Davi fez com eles uma aliança ali, na presença {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, e eles ungiram Davi rei sobre Israel, como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha prometido por meio de Samuel.
pt.R: Todos os líderes de Israel vieram ao rei Davi em Hebrom. Ali Davi fez uma aliança com eles diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, e eles derramaram azeite na cabeça dele para fazê-lo rei sobre Israel. Foi isso o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha dito por meio de Samuel.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 5:3, adding "according to the word of Yahweh by Samuel"
decisions.reason: The verse follows 2 Samuel 5:3, with "David" where Samuel has "King David". Chronicles adds a closing phrase of its own: the anointing happened according to the word of Yahweh through Samuel. It points back to Samuel's anointing of the young David at God's command (1 Samuel 16:1-13), so that the people's choice is shown to carry out what God had already said.

decisions.choice: by the hand of Samuel: through Samuel, as God's messenger
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" a person means through him, as the one who carries a message or does a task (Exodus 9:35; 1 Kings 12:15).

decisions.choice: made a covenant before Yahweh: a binding agreement between the king and the people, with God as witness
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:3. The verb is literally "cut", the usual word for making a covenant. A covenant between a king and his people set out what each owed the other, under oath (1 Samuel 10:25; 2 Kings 11:17).

decisions.choice: leaders; poured oil on his head to make him king
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:3, Readable says "leaders" for "elders", the senior heads of families and tribes, and explains what anointing is.

decisions.choice: as the LORD had promised through Samuel (Balanced); This was what the LORD had said through Samuel (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put "according to the word of the LORD" as a clause, and Readable makes it a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: kwa mkono wa Samweli
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of the hand, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable say "kupitia", the word these drafts use for an agent through whom someone speaks.

decisions.choice: pela mão de Samuel (L); por meio de Samuel (B, R)
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:3 in Portuguese, with "Davi" for "o rei Davi" and the closing phrase Chronicles adds (m1). Literal keeps the Hebrew picture "pela mão de"; Balanced and Readable say "por meio de", what it means (m2).

source.text: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ דָּוִ֧יד וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם הִ֣יא יְב֑וּס וְשָׁם֙ הַיְבוּסִ֔י יֹשְׁבֵ֖י הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went David and all Israel [to] Jerusalem, it [is] Jebus; and there [were] the Jebusites, [the] inhabitants of the land.

en.L: And David and all Israel went [to] Jerusalem, that [is] Jebus; and the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, [were] there.
en.B: Then David and all Israel marched on Jerusalem, that is, Jebus, where the Jebusites lived, the people of that land.
en.R: Then David and all the Israelites went to attack Jerusalem, which was then called Jebus. The Jebusites lived there.

es.L: Y fue David con todo Israel [a] Jerusalén, que [es] Jebús; y allí [estaban] los jebuseos, los habitantes de la tierra.
es.B: Luego David y todo Israel marcharon contra Jerusalén, es decir, Jebús, donde vivían los jebuseos, la gente de aquella tierra.
es.R: Luego David y todos los israelitas fueron a atacar Jerusalén, que entonces se llamaba Jebús. Allí vivían los jebuseos.

fr.L: Et David et tout Israël allèrent [à] Jérusalem, c’[est] Jébus ; et là [étaient] les Jébusiens, les habitants du pays.
fr.B: Puis David et tout Israël marchèrent sur Jérusalem, c’est-à-dire Jébus, où vivaient les Jébusiens, les habitants de ce pays.
fr.R: Ensuite David et tous les Israélites sont allés attaquer Jérusalem, qu’on appelait alors Jébus. Les Jébusiens vivaient là.

sw.L: Daudi na Israeli wote wakaenda Yerusalemu, ndio Yebusi; na Wayebusi, wenyeji wa nchi, [walikuwa] huko.
sw.B: Kisha Daudi na Israeli wote walikwenda kuushambulia Yerusalemu, yaani Yebusi, walikokaa Wayebusi, wenyeji wa nchi ile.
sw.R: Kisha Daudi na Waisraeli wote walikwenda kuushambulia Yerusalemu, ambao wakati huo uliitwa Yebusi. Wayebusi waliishi huko.

vi.L: Đa-vít và tất cả Y-sơ-ra-ên đi [đến] Giê-ru-sa-lem, tức là Giê-bu; người Giê-bu-sít, dân cư trong xứ, [ở] đó.
vi.B: Bấy giờ Đa-vít và tất cả Y-sơ-ra-ên tiến đánh Giê-ru-sa-lem, tức là Giê-bu, nơi người Giê-bu-sít, dân của xứ ấy, sinh sống.
vi.R: Rồi Đa-vít và toàn dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đi đánh Giê-ru-sa-lem, lúc ấy còn gọi là Giê-bu. Người Giê-bu-sít sống ở đó.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗과 온 이스라엘이 예루살렘, 곧 여부스로 갔다. 그리고 거기에는 그 땅의 주민인 여부스 사람들이 [있었다].
ko.B: 그 뒤에 다윗과 온 이스라엘은 예루살렘, 곧 여부스로 진군했다. 그곳에는 그 땅에 사는 여부스 사람들이 있었다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 다윗과 모든 이스라엘 사람은 예루살렘을 치러 갔다. 그때 그 성은 여부스라고 불렸다. 그곳에는 여부스 사람들이 살고 있었다.

pt.L: E Davi e todo o Israel foram [a] Jerusalém, que [é] Jebus; e ali [estavam] os jebuseus, os habitantes da terra.
pt.B: Então Davi e todo o Israel marcharam contra Jerusalém, isto é, Jebus, onde moravam os jebuseus, o povo daquela terra.
pt.R: Então Davi e todos os israelitas foram atacar Jerusalém, que naquele tempo se chamava Jebus. Os jebuseus moravam ali.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 5:6, with "David and all Israel" and "that is, Jebus"
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:6 says "the king and his men" went to Jerusalem, David's own fighting men. Chronicles has "David and all Israel", so the whole nation that has just made him king (verses 1-3) shares in taking the city. It also adds that Jerusalem was then called Jebus, after the Jebusites, as in Joshua 18:28 and Judges 19:10-11.

decisions.choice: the Jebusites: the Canaanite people who still held Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:6. The Jebusites are named among the peoples of Canaan (Genesis 15:21; Deuteronomy 7:1). Neither Judah nor Benjamin had been able to drive them out of Jerusalem (Joshua 15:63; Judges 1:21).

decisions.choice: marched on (Balanced); went to attack (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb is simply "went", but "against" the city is plain from the next verses. Balanced and Readable say so, as in 2 Samuel 5:6. Readable says "which was then called" to show that Jebus is the city's old name.

decisions.choice: "Jébus"
decisions.reason: The old name of Jerusalem in its usual French form, as "les Jébusiens" in 2 Samuel 5:6.

decisions.choice: Jebus; os jebuseus
decisions.reason: "Os jebuseus" as 2 Samuel 5:6 in Portuguese; "Jebus", the old name Chronicles adds (m1), is written as the Hebrew sounds, as Judges 19:10 has it.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ יֹשְׁבֵ֤י יְבוּס֙ לְדָוִ֔יד לֹ֥א תָב֖וֹא הֵ֑נָּה וַיִּלְכֹּ֤ד דָּוִיד֙ אֶת־מְצֻדַ֣ת צִיּ֔וֹן הִ֖יא עִ֥יר דָּוִֽיד׃

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] inhabitants of Jebus to David, Not you will come here. And captured David the stronghold of Zion; it [is the] city of David.

en.L: And the inhabitants of Jebus said to David, "You will not come in here." But David captured the stronghold of Zion; that [is] the City of David.
en.B: The people of Jebus told David, "You will not get in here." But David captured the stronghold of Zion, which is now the City of David.
en.R: The people of Jebus said to David, "You will never get inside this city!" But David captured the fortress of Zion. It became known as the City of David.

es.L: Y los habitantes de Jebús dijeron a David: «No entrarás aquí». Pero David tomó la fortaleza de Sion; esa [es] la ciudad de David.
es.B: Los habitantes de Jebús le dijeron a David: «No entrarás aquí». Pero David tomó la fortaleza de Sion, que ahora es la ciudad de David.
es.R: Los habitantes de Jebús le dijeron a David: «¡Nunca entrarás en esta ciudad!». Pero David conquistó la fortaleza de Sion. Llegó a conocerse como la ciudad de David.

fr.L: Et les habitants de Jébus dirent à David : « Tu n’entreras pas ici. » Mais David s’empara de la forteresse de Sion ; c’[est] la cité de David.
fr.B: Les habitants de Jébus dirent à David : « Tu n’entreras pas ici. » Mais David s’empara de la forteresse de Sion, qui est aujourd’hui la cité de David.
fr.R: Les habitants de Jébus ont dit à David : « Tu n’entreras jamais dans cette ville ! » Mais David s’est emparé de la forteresse de Sion. On l’a appelée ensuite la cité de David.

sw.L: Wenyeji wa Yebusi wakamwambia Daudi, "Hutaingia humu." Lakini Daudi akaiteka ngome ya Sayuni; hiyo [ndiyo] mji wa Daudi.
sw.B: Watu wa Yebusi walimwambia Daudi, "Hutaingia humu." Lakini Daudi aliiteka ngome ya Sayuni, ambayo sasa ni mji wa Daudi.
sw.R: Watu wa Yebusi walimwambia Daudi, "Hutaingia kamwe ndani ya mji huu!" Lakini Daudi aliiteka ngome ya Sayuni. Ikaja kujulikana kama mji wa Daudi.

vi.L: Dân cư Giê-bu nói với Đa-vít: "Ngươi sẽ không vào được đây." Nhưng Đa-vít chiếm được đồn lũy Si-ôn; đó [là] thành Đa-vít.
vi.B: Dân Giê-bu nói với Đa-vít: "Ngươi sẽ không vào được đây đâu." Nhưng Đa-vít chiếm được đồn lũy Si-ôn, nay là thành Đa-vít.
vi.R: Dân Giê-bu nói với Đa-vít: "Ngươi sẽ không bao giờ vào được thành này!" Nhưng Đa-vít chiếm được pháo đài Si-ôn. Nơi ấy được gọi là thành Đa-vít.

ko.L: 그리고 여부스 주민들이 다윗에게 말했다. "너는 여기에 들어오지 못할 것이다." 그러나 다윗이 시온 요새를 점령했다. 그것이 다윗 성[이다].
ko.B: 여부스 주민들이 다윗에게 말했다. "너는 여기에 들어오지 못한다." 그러나 다윗은 시온 요새를 점령했다. 그곳이 지금의 다윗 성이다.
ko.R: 여부스 사람들이 다윗에게 말했다. "너는 절대로 이 성에 들어오지 못한다!" 그러나 다윗은 시온 요새를 빼앗았다. 그곳은 다윗 성이라고 불리게 되었다.

pt.L: E os habitantes de Jebus disseram a Davi: "Você não entrará aqui." Mas Davi tomou a fortaleza de Sião; esta [é] a Cidade de Davi.
pt.B: Os moradores de Jebus disseram a Davi: "Você não vai entrar aqui." Mas Davi tomou a fortaleza de Sião, que agora é a Cidade de Davi.
pt.R: O povo de Jebus disse a Davi: "Você nunca vai entrar nesta cidade!" Mas Davi tomou a fortaleza de Sião. Ela passou a ser conhecida como a Cidade de Davi.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 5:6-7, without the taunt about the blind and the lame
decisions.reason: In 2 Samuel 5:6 the Jebusites boast that even the blind and the lame could keep David out. Chronicles gives only the first words of the boast, "You will not come in here", calls the speakers "the inhabitants of Jebus", and goes straight on to the capture, told in the same words as 2 Samuel 5:7.

decisions.choice: the stronghold of Zion: the fortified hill of the Jebusite city
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:7. Zion was the ridge south of the later temple hill, on which the old city stood. In later books the name comes to mean the whole of Jerusalem, and the place where Yahweh dwells (Psalm 2:6; Isaiah 2:3).

decisions.choice: that is the City of David: a note from the writer's day
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:7, the writer explains the old name by the one his readers knew. Verse 7 tells how the name was given.

decisions.choice: which is now (Balanced); It became known as (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:7, Balanced and Readable show that the name came later. Readable says "fortress" for "stronghold".

decisions.choice: The people of Jebus taunt David in the plain style with "너"
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:6: an enemy's taunt from the walls, where the bare style carries the scorn.

decisions.choice: a fortaleza de Sião; a Cidade de Davi; você (the Jebusites to David)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as 2 Samuel 5:7 in Portuguese: "a fortaleza de Sião" at every level, where the English Readable says "fortress", and "a Cidade de Davi" with a capital, as a name. The Jebusites taunt an enemy, so they say "você", as in 2 Samuel 5:6.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔יד כָּל־מַכֵּ֤ה יְבוּסִי֙ בָּרִ֣אשׁוֹנָ֔ה יִהְיֶ֥ה לְרֹ֖אשׁ וּלְשָׂ֑ר וַיַּ֧עַל בָּרִאשׁוֹנָ֛ה יוֹאָ֥ב בֶּן־צְרוּיָ֖ה וַיְהִ֥י לְרֹֽאשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David, Anyone striking a Jebusite at first will be for chief and for commander. And went up at first Joab son of Zeruiah, and he became chief.

en.L: And David said, "Whoever strikes a Jebusite first will become chief and commander." And Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, and he became chief.
en.B: David had said, "Whoever is first to strike down a Jebusite will become chief and commander." Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, so he became chief.
en.R: David had promised, "The first man to attack the Jebusites will become the chief commander." Joab son of Zeruiah was the first to go up, so he became the chief.

es.L: Y dijo David: «Cualquiera que hiera primero a un jebuseo será jefe y comandante». Y subió primero Joab hijo de Sarvia, y fue hecho jefe.
es.B: David había dicho: «El primero que hiera a un jebuseo será jefe y comandante». Joab hijo de Sarvia subió primero, y así llegó a ser jefe.
es.R: David había prometido: «El primero que ataque a los jebuseos será el comandante en jefe». Joab hijo de Sarvia fue el primero en subir, y así llegó a ser el jefe.

fr.L: Et David dit : « Quiconque frappera un Jébusien le premier deviendra chef et commandant. » Et Joab, fils de Tserouya, monta le premier, et il devint chef.
fr.B: David avait dit : « Celui qui frappera le premier un Jébusien deviendra chef et commandant. » Joab, fils de Tserouya, monta le premier, et il devint chef.
fr.R: David avait promis : « Le premier qui attaquera les Jébusiens deviendra le chef de l’armée. » Joab, fils de Tserouya, est monté le premier, et c’est lui qui est devenu le chef.

sw.L: Daudi akasema, "Yeyote atakayempiga Myebusi kwanza atakuwa mkuu na jemadari." Yoabu mwana wa Seruya akapanda kwanza, akawa mkuu.
sw.B: Daudi alikuwa amesema, "Yeyote atakayekuwa wa kwanza kumpiga Myebusi atakuwa mkuu na jemadari." Yoabu mwana wa Seruya alipanda kwanza, hivyo akawa mkuu.
sw.R: Daudi alikuwa ameahidi, "Mtu wa kwanza kuwashambulia Wayebusi atakuwa kamanda mkuu wa jeshi." Yoabu mwana wa Seruya alikuwa wa kwanza kupanda, hivyo akawa kamanda mkuu.

vi.L: Đa-vít nói: "Ai đánh người Giê-bu-sít trước tiên sẽ làm thủ lĩnh và tướng chỉ huy." Giô-áp con trai Xê-ru-gia đi lên trước tiên, và ông trở thành thủ lĩnh.
vi.B: Đa-vít đã nói: "Ai đánh người Giê-bu-sít trước tiên sẽ được làm thủ lĩnh và tướng chỉ huy." Giô-áp con trai Xê-ru-gia đi lên trước tiên, nên ông được làm thủ lĩnh.
vi.R: Đa-vít đã hứa: "Người nào tấn công người Giê-bu-sít trước tiên sẽ được làm tổng chỉ huy." Giô-áp con trai Xê-ru-gia là người đầu tiên leo lên, nên ông được làm tổng chỉ huy.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 말했다. "누구든지 여부스 사람을 맨 먼저 치는 자는 우두머리와 지휘관이 될 것이다." 그리고 스루야의 아들 요압이 맨 먼저 올라가서 우두머리가 되었다.
ko.B: 다윗은 "누구든지 여부스 사람을 맨 먼저 쳐 죽이는 사람은 우두머리와 지휘관이 될 것이다" 하고 말해 두었다. 스루야의 아들 요압이 맨 먼저 올라갔으므로 그가 우두머리가 되었다.
ko.R: 다윗은 미리 이렇게 약속했었다. "여부스 사람들을 맨 먼저 공격하는 사람을 군대의 총사령관으로 삼겠다." 스루야의 아들 요압이 맨 먼저 올라갔다. 그래서 그가 총사령관이 되었다.

pt.L: E Davi disse: "Todo aquele que ferir primeiro um jebuseu será chefe e comandante." E Joabe, filho de Zeruia, subiu primeiro, e se tornou chefe.
pt.B: Davi tinha dito: "Quem for o primeiro a matar um jebuseu será chefe e comandante." Joabe, filho de Zeruia, subiu primeiro e por isso se tornou chefe.
pt.R: Davi tinha prometido: "O primeiro homem que atacar os jebuseus vai ser o comandante-chefe." Joabe, filho de Zeruia, foi o primeiro a subir, e por isso se tornou o chefe.

decisions.choice: in place of 2 Samuel 5:8: Joab goes up first and becomes chief; no water shaft and no saying about the blind and the lame
decisions.reason: In 2 Samuel 5:8 David gives an unfinished order about reaching the defenders by the water shaft, and the writer explains a saying about the blind and the lame. Chronicles has neither. It gives instead David's promise of the chief command to the first man to strike the Jebusites, and tells that Joab son of Zeruiah went up first and won it. This may be the promise that the broken sentence in Samuel seems to lack.

decisions.choice: David said: the promise came before the capture told in verse 5
decisions.reason: Verse 5 tells the capture in one short clause; verse 6 goes back to tell how it was done. David's words were spoken before the attack.

decisions.choice: chief and commander: head of David's army
decisions.reason: "Chief" is literally "head", and "commander" is the usual word for an officer. Together they mean the top command of the army, the post Joab holds in 18:15 and 27:34. Joab is already leading David's men in 2 Samuel 2:13; Chronicles tells how his command over the whole army began.

decisions.choice: went up: climbed up into the city on its hill
decisions.reason: Jerusalem stood on a ridge, so attackers "went up" against it. The word may also look to the water shaft of 2 Samuel 5:8, but Chronicles does not say how Joab got in.

decisions.choice: David had said (Balanced); David had promised (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the promise was made before the capture, as m2 explains. Readable puts "chief and commander" as "the chief commander", one post.

decisions.choice: "David avait dit" (B); "David avait promis" (R), plus-que-parfait
decisions.reason: French marks with the plus-que-parfait that the promise came before the capture told in verse 5, as the English Balanced and Readable do with "had said".

decisions.choice: alikuwa amesema (B); alikuwa ameahidi (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the past perfect, as the English does, because David's promise came before the capture already told in verse 5.

decisions.choice: "thủ lĩnh và tướng chỉ huy" (L, B); "tổng chỉ huy" (R)
decisions.reason: "Head" here is the top command of the army, so it is "thủ lĩnh" rather than the body word; Readable makes the pair one post, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "말해 두었다" (B), "미리 이렇게 약속했었다" (R)
decisions.reason: The promise was made before the capture told in verse 5, as the English Balanced and Readable show; Korean marks it with an aspect ending (B) and "미리" with the past perfect (R).

decisions.choice: Davi tinha dito / tinha prometido (B, R); o comandante-chefe (R)
decisions.reason: The pluperfect "tinha dito" shows, as the English "had said" does, that the promise came before the capture of verse 5 (m2). Readable joins "chief and commander" in "comandante-chefe", the Portuguese word for the top command (m3).

source.text: וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב דָּוִ֖יד בַּמְצָ֑ד עַל־כֵּ֥ן קָרְאוּ־ל֖וֹ עִ֥יר דָּוִֽיד׃

records.literal_gloss: And dwelt David in the stronghold; therefore they called it [the] city of David.

en.L: And David lived in the stronghold; therefore they called it the City of David.
en.B: David took up residence in the stronghold, and that is why it was called the City of David.
en.R: David made his home in the fortress, so people called it the City of David.

es.L: Y habitó David en la fortaleza; por eso la llamaron la ciudad de David.
es.B: David se estableció en la fortaleza, y por eso se la llamó la ciudad de David.
es.R: David se fue a vivir a la fortaleza, y por eso la gente la llamó la ciudad de David.

fr.L: Et David habita dans la forteresse ; c’est pourquoi on l’appela la cité de David.
fr.B: David s’installa dans la forteresse, et c’est pourquoi on l’appela la cité de David.
fr.R: David est allé habiter dans la forteresse, et c’est pour cela qu’on l’a appelée la cité de David.

sw.L: Daudi akakaa ngomeni; kwa hiyo wakauita mji wa Daudi.
sw.B: Daudi alifanya makao yake katika ngome hiyo, na ndiyo sababu uliitwa mji wa Daudi.
sw.R: Daudi alifanya makao yake katika ngome hiyo, kwa hiyo watu wakauita mji wa Daudi.

vi.L: Đa-vít ở trong đồn lũy; vì thế người ta gọi nơi ấy là thành Đa-vít.
vi.B: Đa-vít đến ở trong đồn lũy, và vì thế nơi ấy được gọi là thành Đa-vít.
vi.R: Đa-vít ở trong pháo đài, nên người ta gọi nơi ấy là thành Đa-vít.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 그 요새에 살았다. 그래서 사람들이 그곳을 다윗 성이라고 불렀다.
ko.B: 다윗이 그 요새에 자리 잡고 살았으므로, 그곳을 다윗 성이라고 부르게 되었다.
ko.R: 다윗이 그 요새에서 살았다. 그래서 사람들은 그곳을 다윗 성이라고 불렀다.

pt.L: E Davi habitou na fortaleza; por isso a chamaram Cidade de Davi.
pt.B: Davi passou a morar na fortaleza, e é por isso que ela foi chamada Cidade de Davi.
pt.R: Davi foi morar na fortaleza, e por isso o povo a chamou de Cidade de Davi.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 5:9a, with "therefore they called it" in place of "and he called it"
decisions.reason: In 2 Samuel 5:9 David himself names the stronghold. Chronicles says that people called it the City of David because he lived there. Chronicles also uses a shorter form of the word for "stronghold" here, with the same meaning.

decisions.choice: they called: people in general called it
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject. "They" means people in general, so the name came from common use.

decisions.choice: it was called
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the verb with no stated subject as a passive; Readable says "people".

decisions.choice: a chamaram (L); foi chamada (B); o povo a chamou (R)
decisions.reason: As 2 Samuel 5:9 in Portuguese ("habitou", "passou a morar", "foi morar na fortaleza"), but the naming has no stated subject here (m1, m2): Literal keeps the impersonal plural, Balanced a passive and Readable "o povo", as the English levels do.

source.text: וַיִּ֤בֶן הָעִיר֙ מִסָּבִ֔יב מִן־הַמִּלּ֖וֹא וְעַד־הַסָּבִ֑יב וְיוֹאָ֕ב יְחַיֶּ֖ה אֶת־שְׁאָ֥ר הָעִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he built the city from round about, from the Millo and to the surrounding; and Joab restored [the] rest of the city.

en.L: And he built the city all around, from the Millo even to the surrounding [area]; and Joab restored the rest of the city.
en.B: He built up the city all around, from the Millo to the area around it, and Joab repaired the rest of the city.
en.R: David built up the city all around, from the Millo (a supporting terrace) out to the area around it. Joab repaired the rest of the city.

es.L: Y edificó la ciudad alrededor, desde el Milo hasta los alrededores; y Joab restauró el resto de la ciudad.
es.B: Edificó la ciudad por todos lados, desde el Milo hasta la zona de alrededor, y Joab reparó el resto de la ciudad.
es.R: David construyó la ciudad por todos lados, desde el Milo (una terraza de apoyo) hasta la zona de alrededor. Joab reparó el resto de la ciudad.

fr.L: Et il bâtit la ville tout autour, depuis le Millo jusqu’aux alentours ; et Joab restaura le reste de la ville.
fr.B: Il construisit la ville tout autour, depuis le Millo jusqu’aux environs, et Joab répara le reste de la ville.
fr.R: David a construit la ville tout autour, depuis le Millo (une grande terrasse de soutien) jusqu’aux environs. Joab a réparé le reste de la ville.

sw.L: Akaujenga mji pande zote, kuanzia Milo hata [eneo] la kuzunguka; naye Yoabu akaitengeneza sehemu iliyobaki ya mji.
sw.B: Aliujenga mji pande zote, kuanzia Milo mpaka eneo lililouzunguka, naye Yoabu akaikarabati sehemu iliyobaki ya mji.
sw.R: Daudi aliujenga mji pande zote, kuanzia Milo (matuta ya mawe yaliyoshikilia ukuta) mpaka eneo lililouzunguka. Yoabu akaikarabati sehemu iliyobaki ya mji.

vi.L: Ông xây thành chung quanh, từ Mi-lô cho đến khu chung quanh; còn Giô-áp thì sửa lại phần còn lại của thành.
vi.B: Ông xây dựng thành chung quanh, từ Mi-lô đến khu vực bao quanh, còn Giô-áp thì tu sửa phần còn lại của thành.
vi.R: Đa-vít xây dựng thành chung quanh, từ Mi-lô (một nền đất đắp cao) ra đến khu vực chung quanh. Giô-áp tu sửa phần còn lại của thành.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 밀로에서부터 사방으로 둘러 성을 쌓았고, 요압은 성의 나머지 부분을 되살렸다.
ko.B: 그는 밀로에서부터 그 주변까지 사방으로 성을 쌓았고, 요압은 성의 나머지 부분을 보수했다.
ko.R: 다윗은 밀로에서부터 그 주변까지 성을 빙 둘러 쌓았다. 밀로는 흙과 돌로 쌓은 받침대였다. 요압은 성의 나머지 부분을 고쳤다.

pt.L: E ele construiu a cidade ao redor, desde o Milo até os arredores; e Joabe restaurou o resto da cidade.
pt.B: Ele construiu a cidade ao redor, desde o Milo até a área em volta, e Joabe reparou o resto da cidade.
pt.R: Davi construiu a cidade ao redor, desde o Milo (um grande aterro de sustentação) até a área em volta. Joabe consertou o resto da cidade.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 5:9b, adding that Joab repaired the rest of the city
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:9 says that David built "all around, from the Millo and inward". Chronicles says that he built "the city", "from the Millo to the surrounding area", and adds that Joab restored the rest of the city. Joab, now chief (verse 6), shares in the work.

decisions.choice: the Millo: probably a terrace of built-up earth and stone
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:9. The name comes from the verb "to fill", so it probably means a great terrace or rampart of packed earth and stone on the steep slope. Its exact form and place are not known.

decisions.choice: restored: repaired, rebuilt what was damaged
decisions.reason: The verb is "make live". Used of a city or of stones it means to bring back into use what lay ruined (Nehemiah 3:34). Joab repaired the parts of the city not covered by David's own building.

decisions.choice: David; the Millo (a supporting terrace)
decisions.reason: Readable names David as the builder, to keep him apart from Joab, and explains the Millo briefly, as in 2 Samuel 5:9.

decisions.choice: "되살렸다"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture "made live", used of bringing ruined walls back into use; Balanced and Readable say "repaired".

decisions.choice: o Milo; um grande aterro de sustentação (R); restaurou (L), reparou (B), consertou (R)
decisions.reason: "O Milo" and Readable's explanation as 2 Samuel 5:9 in Portuguese. The verb is "make live" (m3); Literal says "restaurou", bringing back into use, and Balanced and Readable say plainly that Joab repaired the rest.

source.text: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִ֖יד הָל֣וֹךְ וְגָד֑וֹל וַיהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת עִמּֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And went David going and great, and Yahweh of hosts [was] with him.

en.L: And David went on becoming greater and greater, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts [was] with him.
en.B: David became greater and greater, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies was with him.
en.R: David became more and more powerful, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies was with him.

es.L: Y David iba engrandeciéndose más y más, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos [estaba] con él.
es.B: David se hacía cada vez más grande, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos estaba con él.
es.R: David se hacía cada vez más poderoso, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos estaba con él.

fr.L: Et David allait en grandissant de plus en plus, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées [était] avec lui.
fr.B: David devint de plus en plus grand, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées était avec lui.
fr.R: David est devenu de plus en plus puissant, parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées était avec lui.

sw.L: Daudi akazidi kuwa mkuu zaidi na zaidi, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi [alikuwa] pamoja naye.
sw.B: Daudi alizidi kuwa mkuu zaidi na zaidi, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi alikuwa pamoja naye.
sw.R: Daudi alizidi kuwa na nguvu zaidi na zaidi, kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi alikuwa pamoja naye.

vi.L: Đa-vít càng ngày càng lớn mạnh, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân [ở] với ông.
vi.B: Đa-vít ngày càng hùng mạnh, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân ở với ông.
vi.R: Đa-vít ngày càng hùng mạnh, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân ở với ông.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 점점 더 커졌으니, 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그와 함께 [계셨다].
ko.B: 다윗은 점점 강대해졌다. 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그와 함께 계셨기 때문이다.
ko.R: 다윗은 점점 더 강해졌다. 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그와 함께 계셨기 때문이다.

pt.L: E Davi foi se tornando cada vez maior, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos [estava] com ele.
pt.B: Davi se tornava cada vez maior, porque {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos estava com ele.
pt.R: Davi foi ficando cada vez mais poderoso, porque {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos estava com ele.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 5:10, with "Yahweh of hosts" in place of "Yahweh, God of hosts"
decisions.reason: Chronicles has the shorter, more usual form of the title, without "God". Otherwise the verse is the same as 2 Samuel 5:10.

decisions.choice: went going and great: grew steadily greater
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:10. The verb "go" with a second verb describes something that keeps on happening (Genesis 26:13; 1 Samuel 2:26).

decisions.choice: Yahweh of hosts was with him: the reason for David's rise
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 5:10. David's success comes from God's presence (1 Samuel 16:18; 18:14). The title means Yahweh, commander of the armies of heaven and earth (1 Samuel 1:3).

decisions.choice: for, because; the LORD of Armies
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the second clause gives the reason, and say "Armies" for "hosts", as in the rest of these books.

decisions.choice: el SEÑOR de los ejércitos (L); el SEÑOR de los Ejércitos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Psalms note gives "el SEÑOR de los ejércitos" at Literal and "de los Ejércitos" at Balanced and Readable; Chronicles has no "God of" here, unlike 2 Samuel 5:10.

decisions.choice: BWANA wa majeshi
decisions.reason: Chronicles has "Yahweh of hosts" where 2 Samuel 5:10 has "Yahweh, God of hosts"; the Swahili follows the shorter title, in its usual form "BWANA wa majeshi" at every level.

decisions.choice: "CHÚA Vạn Quân"
decisions.reason: The Samuel note's form for "the LORD of hosts", the span on CHÚA only; Chronicles has no "God of" here, unlike 2 Samuel 5:10, so the Vietnamese drops "Đức Chúa Trời".

decisions.choice: "만군의 주" (L, B); "하늘의 군대를 거느리신 주" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for "the LORD of hosts"; Chronicles has the title without "God", so the Korean drops "하나님" from the wording of 2 Samuel 5:10.

decisions.choice: o SENHOR dos Exércitos
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 5:10 in Portuguese, with the shorter title Chronicles has (m1): "o SENHOR dos Exércitos", the book-wide form of 1 Samuel 1:3, instead of "o SENHOR, o Deus dos Exércitos".

source.text: וְאֵ֨לֶּה רָאשֵׁ֤י הַגִּבּוֹרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְדָוִ֔יד הַמִּתְחַזְּקִ֨ים עִמּ֧וֹ בְמַלְכוּת֛וֹ עִם־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְהַמְלִיכ֑וֹ כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And these [are the] chiefs of the mighty men who [belonged] to David, the [ones] strengthening themselves with him in his kingdom with all Israel to make him king, according to [the] word of Yahweh concerning Israel.

en.L: And these [are] the chiefs of the mighty men whom David had, who held strongly with him in his kingdom, together with all Israel, to make him king, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} concerning Israel.
en.B: These are the chiefs of David's mighty warriors, who gave him strong support in his kingdom, together with all Israel, to make him king, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had promised concerning Israel.
en.R: These were the leaders of David's best warriors. Together with all Israel, they gave strong support to his rule and helped make him king. This was what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had promised about Israel.

es.L: Y estos [son] los jefes de los valientes que tenía David, que se mantuvieron firmes con él en su reino, junto con todo Israel, para hacerlo rey, conforme a la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} acerca de Israel.
es.B: Estos son los jefes de los guerreros valientes de David, que le dieron un firme apoyo en su reino, junto con todo Israel, para hacerlo rey, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo había prometido acerca de Israel.
es.R: Estos eran los jefes de los mejores guerreros de David. Junto con todo Israel, apoyaron con fuerza su reinado y ayudaron a hacerlo rey. Esto era lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había prometido acerca de Israel.

fr.L: Et voici les chefs des vaillants hommes qu’avait David, qui le soutinrent fortement dans son règne, avec tout Israël, pour le faire roi, selon la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} au sujet d’Israël.
fr.B: Voici les chefs des vaillants guerriers de David, qui lui apportèrent un ferme soutien dans son règne, avec tout Israël, pour le faire roi, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait promis au sujet d’Israël.
fr.R: Voici les chefs des meilleurs guerriers de David. Avec tout Israël, ils ont fermement soutenu son règne et ils l’ont aidé à devenir roi. C’était ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait promis au sujet d’Israël.

sw.L: Hawa [ndio] wakuu wa mashujaa aliokuwa nao Daudi, waliojitia nguvu pamoja naye katika ufalme wake, pamoja na Israeli wote, ili kumfanya mfalme, sawasawa na neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kuhusu Israeli.
sw.B: Hawa ndio wakuu wa mashujaa wa Daudi, waliomuunga mkono kwa nguvu katika ufalme wake, pamoja na Israeli wote, ili kumfanya mfalme, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyoahidi kuhusu Israeli.
sw.R: Hawa ndio waliokuwa viongozi wa wapiganaji hodari kuliko wote wa Daudi. Pamoja na Israeli wote, waliuunga mkono kwa nguvu utawala wake na kusaidia kumfanya mfalme. Ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa ameahidi kuhusu Israeli.

vi.L: Đây [là] các thủ lĩnh của các dũng sĩ mà Đa-vít có, là những người hết sức ủng hộ ông trong vương quốc của ông, cùng với tất cả Y-sơ-ra-ên, để lập ông làm vua, theo lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} về Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Đây là các thủ lĩnh trong hàng dũng sĩ của Đa-vít, những người đã hết lòng ủng hộ vương quyền của ông, cùng với tất cả Y-sơ-ra-ên, để lập ông làm vua, đúng như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã hứa về Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Đây là những người lãnh đạo các chiến binh giỏi nhất của Đa-vít. Cùng với toàn dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, họ hết sức ủng hộ ông và giúp lập ông làm vua. Việc này đúng như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã hứa về Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗에게 있던 용사들의 우두머리들은 이러하다. 그들은 이스라엘에 관한 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀대로, 그를 왕으로 세우려고 그의 나라에서 온 이스라엘과 함께 그와 더불어 힘을 다해 섰다.
ko.B: 다윗의 용사들의 우두머리들은 이러하다. 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘에 관하여 약속하신 대로, 온 이스라엘과 함께 다윗의 나라에서 그를 힘써 도와 그를 왕으로 세웠다.
ko.R: 다윗의 가장 뛰어난 용사들의 지도자들은 이러했다. 그들은 모든 이스라엘 사람과 함께 다윗의 나라를 힘껏 도왔고, 그를 왕으로 세우는 일을 도왔다. 이것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘에 관하여 약속하신 일이었다.

pt.L: E estes [são] os chefes dos valentes que Davi tinha, que se mantiveram firmes com ele no seu reino, junto com todo o Israel, para fazê-lo rei, conforme a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} a respeito de Israel.
pt.B: Estes são os chefes dos guerreiros de Davi, que lhe deram firme apoio no seu reino, junto com todo o Israel, para fazê-lo rei, como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha prometido a respeito de Israel.
pt.R: Estes eram os líderes dos melhores guerreiros de Davi. Junto com todo o Israel, eles deram firme apoio ao seu governo e ajudaram a fazê-lo rei. Foi isso o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha prometido a respeito de Israel.

decisions.choice: a heading of Chronicles' own for the list of 2 Samuel 23:8-39
decisions.reason: In Samuel the list of David's warriors stands near the end of his story, after his last words (2 Samuel 23:1-7). Chronicles places it at the start of his reign and gives it this heading, which ties the warriors to his being made king by all Israel (verses 1-3).

decisions.choice: held strongly with him: put their strength behind him, gave him firm support
decisions.reason: The verb is a form of "be strong" that means to show oneself strong; with "with him" it means to stand firmly on someone's side.

decisions.choice: according to the word of Yahweh concerning Israel: the warriors' support carries out God's promise
decisions.reason: The phrase repeats the end of verse 3. The men who made David king did what Yahweh had said about Israel, that David would shepherd his people (verse 2).

decisions.choice: mighty warriors (Balanced); best warriors (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:8: Literal keeps "mighty men", Balanced says "mighty warriors" and Readable "best warriors" through the chapter.

decisions.choice: los valientes (L); los guerreros valientes (B); los mejores guerreros (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as the Spanish list of 2 Samuel 23, which this chapter retells.

decisions.choice: "vaillants guerriers" (B); "meilleurs guerriers" (R)
decisions.reason: As 2 Samuel 23 in French, so the two lists of David’s warriors read alike.

decisions.choice: mashujaa (L, B); wapiganaji hodari kuliko wote (R)
decisions.reason: As 2 Samuel 23, "mashujaa" names David's mighty men at Literal and Balanced, and Readable says plainly "his best fighters"; the same wording runs through the list.

decisions.choice: "dũng sĩ" (L, B); "chiến binh giỏi nhất" (R)
decisions.reason: The words of the Vietnamese 2 Samuel 23 for David's mighty men, kept through this list.

decisions.choice: "용사들" (L, B); "가장 뛰어난 용사들" (R)
decisions.reason: As 2 Samuel 23:8 in Korean, kept through the list of chapter 11.

decisions.choice: os valentes de Davi (L); os guerreiros (B); os melhores guerreiros (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: David's company of warriors keeps the words of 2 Samuel 23:8-39 in Portuguese, the list Chronicles retells: "os valentes" at Literal, "os guerreiros" at Balanced and "os melhores guerreiros" at Readable, through verse 47.

source.text: וְאֵ֛לֶּה מִסְפַּ֥ר הַגִּבֹּרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְדָוִ֑יד יָשָׁבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־חַכְמוֹנִ֗י רֹ֚אשׁ הַשָּׁ֣לִישִׁ֔ים הֽוּא־עוֹרֵ֧ר אֶת־חֲנִית֛וֹ עַל־שְׁלֹשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת חָלָ֖ל בְּפַ֥עַם אֶחָֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And these [are the] number of the mighty men who [belonged] to David: Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, chief of the Thirty; he wielded his spear against three hundred slain at one time.

en.L: And this [is] the count of the mighty men whom David had: Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, chief of the Thirty; he wielded his spear against three hundred slain at one time.
en.B: This is the roll of David's mighty warriors. Jashobeam son of Hachmoni was chief of the Thirty. He raised his spear against three hundred men and killed them at one time.
en.R: Here is the list of David's best warriors. Jashobeam son of Hachmoni was the leader of the Thirty. In one battle he fought three hundred men with his spear and killed them.

es.L: Y esta [es] la cuenta de los valientes que tenía David: Jasobeam hijo de Hacmoni, jefe de los Treinta; él blandió su lanza contra trescientos muertos de una vez.
es.B: Esta es la lista de los guerreros valientes de David. Jasobeam hijo de Hacmoni era el jefe de los Treinta. Levantó su lanza contra trescientos hombres y los mató de una vez.
es.R: Esta es la lista de los mejores guerreros de David. Jasobeam hijo de Hacmoni era el líder de los Treinta. En una sola batalla peleó con su lanza contra trescientos hombres y los mató.

fr.L: Et voici le nombre des vaillants hommes qu’avait David : Yashobeam, fils de Hakmoni, chef des Trente ; il brandit sa lance contre trois cents tués en une seule fois.
fr.B: Voici la liste des vaillants guerriers de David. Yashobeam, fils de Hakmoni, était le chef des Trente. Il brandit sa lance contre trois cents hommes et les tua en une seule fois.
fr.R: Voici la liste des meilleurs guerriers de David. Yashobeam, fils de Hakmoni, était le chef des Trente. Dans une seule bataille, il a combattu trois cents hommes avec sa lance et il les a tués.

sw.L: Na hii [ndiyo] hesabu ya mashujaa aliokuwa nao Daudi: Yashobeamu mwana wa Hakmoni, mkuu wa wale Thelathini; yeye aliuinua mkuki wake dhidi ya watu mia tatu waliouawa wakati mmoja.
sw.B: Hii ndiyo orodha ya mashujaa wa Daudi. Yashobeamu mwana wa Hakmoni alikuwa mkuu wa wale Thelathini. Aliuinua mkuki wake dhidi ya watu mia tatu akawaua wakati mmoja.
sw.R: Hii ndiyo orodha ya wapiganaji hodari kuliko wote wa Daudi. Yashobeamu mwana wa Hakmoni alikuwa kiongozi wa wale Thelathini. Katika vita kimoja alipigana na watu mia tatu kwa mkuki wake akawaua.

vi.L: Đây [là] danh sách các dũng sĩ mà Đa-vít có: Gia-sô-bê-am con trai Hác-mô-ni, thủ lĩnh của nhóm Ba Mươi; ông vung giáo chống lại ba trăm người bị giết trong một lần.
vi.B: Đây là danh sách các dũng sĩ của Đa-vít. Gia-sô-bê-am con trai Hác-mô-ni là thủ lĩnh của nhóm Ba Mươi. Ông vung giáo đánh ba trăm người và giết họ trong một trận.
vi.R: Đây là danh sách những chiến binh giỏi nhất của Đa-vít. Gia-sô-bê-am con trai Hác-mô-ni là người lãnh đạo nhóm Ba Mươi. Trong một trận đánh, ông dùng giáo đánh ba trăm người và giết họ.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗에게 있던 용사들의 수는 이러하다. 학몬의 아들 야소브암은 삼십 인의 우두머리였다. 그는 창을 휘둘러 한꺼번에 삼백 명을 [맞서] 죽였다.
ko.B: 다윗의 용사들의 명단은 이러하다. 학몬의 아들 야소브암은 삼십 인의 우두머리였다. 그는 창을 휘둘러 삼백 명과 싸워 한꺼번에 그들을 죽였다.
ko.R: 다윗의 가장 뛰어난 용사들의 명단은 이러하다. 학몬의 아들 야소브암은 삼십 용사의 지도자였다. 그는 한 싸움에서 창으로 삼백 명과 싸워 그들을 죽였다.

pt.L: E esta [é] a contagem dos valentes que Davi tinha: Jasobeão, filho de Hacmoni, chefe dos Trinta; ele brandiu a sua lança contra trezentos mortos de uma vez.
pt.B: Esta é a lista dos guerreiros de Davi. Jasobeão, filho de Hacmoni, era o chefe dos Trinta. Ele ergueu a sua lança contra trezentos homens e os matou de uma só vez.
pt.R: Aqui está a lista dos melhores guerreiros de Davi. Jasobeão, filho de Hacmoni, era o líder dos Trinta. Numa só batalha ele lutou com a sua lança contra trezentos homens e os matou.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 23:8, with the name Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, "he wielded his spear", and three hundred in place of eight hundred
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 23:8 names this man Josheb-Basshebeth the Tahchemonite and adds "he was Adino the Eznite" without a verb for the fighting. Chronicles gives the name as Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, the form used for a commander in 27:2, and has "he wielded his spear", which gives a clear sense. It also counts three hundred slain where Samuel has eight hundred; three hundred is also the number for Abishai (verse 20). Samuel's "names" is "count" here.

decisions.choice: chief of the Thirty: the written text; the spoken reading is "chief of the officers"
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew letters give "the Thirty", the group this list names (verses 15, 25, 42). The scribes' marginal reading, to be read aloud, gives "the officers", picked men close to the king, as in 2 Samuel 23:8; its letters can also be read "the Three". Here the written form is followed. Either way Jashobeam heads David's warriors.

decisions.choice: the count: the list, the roll
decisions.reason: The word means a number or count, here the roll of names that follows.

decisions.choice: the Thirty (capital T)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23, where "the Three" or "the Thirty" stands alone as the name of a group of warriors, every level writes it with a capital letter, so the reader can tell the group from the number.

decisions.choice: and killed them
decisions.reason: "Against three hundred slain" means he fought them and they fell by his hand, so Balanced and Readable supply "killed", as in 2 Samuel 23:8, 18.

decisions.choice: Jasobeam hijo de Hacmoni; los Treinta, los Tres (capitals)
decisions.reason: Names in the usual Spanish forms, kept apart from the "Joseb-basebet" of 2 Samuel 23:8, since the Hebrew names differ; "los Treinta" and "los Tres" are capitalized as titles of the two bands, as in the Spanish of 2 Samuel 23.

decisions.choice: "Yashobeam, fils de Hakmoni"
decisions.reason: Names not found in Samuel are transcribed from the Hebrew in the same way as the French of 2 Samuel 23 ("y" for the Hebrew y, "k" for k), so the lists read as one.

decisions.choice: wale Thelathini; wale Watatu
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23, the two ranks of warriors are written with a capital and "wale" ("those"), so the reader sees a named group and not a plain number.

decisions.choice: "nhóm Ba Mươi"; "nhóm Ba"
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese 2 Samuel 23 names the two ranks of warriors "nhóm Ba Mươi" and "nhóm Ba", capitalised as titles; this list keeps them.

decisions.choice: "삼십 인" (L, B) and "삼십 용사" (R) for the company called the Thirty; "세 용사" for the Three
decisions.reason: As 2 Samuel 23:13 in Korean: the English marks these companies with capitals, Korean has none, so each has a fixed name, kept through the chapter.

decisions.choice: names of David's warriors in the traditional Korean Protestant spellings (학몬, 야소브암, and so on through verse 47)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23: the names follow the forms Korean readers know; where Chronicles spells a name differently from Samuel, the Korean follows Chronicles.

decisions.choice: Jasobeão, filho de Hacmoni; os Trinta; brandiu a sua lança contra trezentos
decisions.reason: Chronicles names the man differently from 2 Samuel 23:8 ("Josebe-Bassebete, o taquemonita") and gives three hundred, not eight hundred (m1), so the names and number change; the rest keeps 2 Samuel 23:8 and 18 in Portuguese ("brandiu", "ergueu a sua lança ... e os matou"). "Os Trinta" with a capital, as in 2 Samuel 23:13.

source.text: וְאַחֲרָ֛יו אֶלְעָזָ֥ר בֶּן־דּוֹד֖וֹ הָאֲחוֹחִ֑י ה֖וּא בִּשְׁלוֹשָׁ֥ה הַגִּבֹּרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And after him Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite; he [was] among [the] three the mighty men.

en.L: And after him [was] Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite; he [was] among the three mighty men.
en.B: Next to him was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite. He was one of the three mighty warriors.
en.R: Next came Eleazar son of Dodo from the clan of Ahoah. He was one of the three best warriors.

es.L: Y después de él [estaba] Eleazar hijo de Dodo el ahohíta; él [era] de los tres valientes.
es.B: Después de él venía Eleazar hijo de Dodo el ahohíta. Era uno de los tres guerreros valientes.
es.R: Después venía Eleazar hijo de Dodo, del clan de Ahoa. Era uno de los tres mejores guerreros.

fr.L: Et après lui [venait] Éléazar, fils de Dodo, l’Ahohite ; il [était] parmi les trois vaillants hommes.
fr.B: Après lui venait Éléazar, fils de Dodo l’Ahohite. Il était l’un des trois vaillants guerriers.
fr.R: Ensuite venait Éléazar, fils de Dodo, du clan d’Ahoah. C’était l’un des trois meilleurs guerriers.

sw.L: Na baada yake [alikuwa] Eleazari mwana wa Dodo Mwahohi; yeye [alikuwa] miongoni mwa wale mashujaa watatu.
sw.B: Aliyefuata baada yake alikuwa Eleazari mwana wa Dodo Mwahohi. Yeye alikuwa mmoja wa wale mashujaa watatu.
sw.R: Aliyefuata alikuwa Eleazari mwana wa Dodo, wa ukoo wa Ahohi. Yeye alikuwa mmoja wa wale wapiganaji watatu hodari kuliko wote.

vi.L: Sau ông [là] Ê-lê-a-xa con trai Đô-đô người A-hô-a; ông [ở] trong ba dũng sĩ.
vi.B: Kế đến là Ê-lê-a-xa con trai Đô-đô người A-hô-a. Ông là một trong ba dũng sĩ.
vi.R: Kế đến là Ê-lê-a-xa con trai Đô-đô, thuộc dòng họ A-hô-a. Ông là một trong ba chiến binh giỏi nhất.

ko.L: 그리고 그다음은 아호아 사람 도도의 아들 엘르아살이었다. 그는 세 용사 가운데 하나였다.
ko.B: 그다음은 아호아 사람 도도의 아들 엘르아살이었다. 그는 세 용사 가운데 하나였다.
ko.R: 그다음은 아호아 집안 도도의 아들 엘르아살이었다. 그는 가장 뛰어난 용사 세 사람 가운데 하나였다.

pt.L: E depois dele, Eleazar, filho de Dodô, o aoíta; ele [estava] entre os três valentes.
pt.B: Depois dele vinha Eleazar, filho de Dodô, o aoíta. Ele era um dos três guerreiros.
pt.R: Depois vinha Eleazar, filho de Dodô, do clã de Aoá. Ele era um dos três melhores guerreiros.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 23:9a, with "the Ahohite" for "son of an Ahohite"
decisions.reason: The words follow 2 Samuel 23:9 up to "the three mighty men". Samuel's next words, about taunting the Philistines, are told differently in verse 13.

decisions.choice: the three mighty men: the Three, who stood above David's other warriors
decisions.reason: In 2 Samuel 23:8-12 the Three are Josheb-Basshebeth, Eleazar and Shammah. Chronicles names only Jashobeam and Eleazar; Shammah's deed is missing (see verse 13).

decisions.choice: from the clan of Ahoah
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:9, Readable explains "the Ahohite", a man of the family of Ahoah, a descendant of Benjamin (8:4).

decisions.choice: Eleazar, filho de Dodô, o aoíta (L, B); do clã de Aoá (R)
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 23:9 in Portuguese up to "os três valentes" (m1), with "o aoíta" at Literal for Chronicles' "the Ahohite" where Samuel has "filho de um aoíta".

source.text: הֽוּא־הָיָ֨ה עִם־דָּוִ֜יד בַּפַּ֣ס דַּמִּ֗ים וְהַפְּלִשְׁתִּים֙ נֶאֱסְפוּ־שָׁ֣םלַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וַתְּהִ֛י חֶלְקַ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה מְלֵאָ֣ה שְׂעוֹרִ֑ים וְהָעָ֥ם נָ֖סוּ מִפְּנֵ֥י פְלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: He was with David at Pas-dammim, and the Philistines were gathered there for battle; and was a plot of the field full [of] barley, and the people fled from before [the] Philistines.

en.L: He was with David at Pas-dammim when the Philistines were gathered there for battle, and there was a plot of the field full of barley; and the people fled before [the] Philistines.
en.B: He was with David at Pas-dammim when the Philistines had gathered there for battle. There was a plot of land full of barley, and the troops ran from the Philistines.
en.R: He was with David at Pas-dammim, where the Philistines had gathered for battle. There was a field there full of barley, and the army of Israel ran away from the Philistines.

es.L: Él estaba con David en Pas-damim, cuando los filisteos se habían reunido allí para la batalla; y había una parcela del campo llena de cebada, y el pueblo huyó delante de los filisteos.
es.B: Estaba con David en Pas-damim cuando los filisteos se habían reunido allí para la batalla. Había una parcela llena de cebada, y la tropa huyó delante de los filisteos.
es.R: Estaba con David en Pas-damim, donde los filisteos se habían reunido para la batalla. Allí había un campo lleno de cebada, y el ejército de Israel huyó de los filisteos.

fr.L: Il était avec David à Pas-Dammim, et les Philistins s’étaient rassemblés là pour le combat ; et il y avait une parcelle de champ pleine d’orge, et le peuple s’enfuit devant les Philistins.
fr.B: Il était avec David à Pas-Dammim, quand les Philistins s’y étaient rassemblés pour le combat. Il y avait là une parcelle pleine d’orge, et la troupe s’enfuit devant les Philistins.
fr.R: Il était avec David à Pas-Dammim, où les Philistins s’étaient rassemblés pour combattre. Il y avait là un champ plein d’orge, et l’armée d’Israël s’est enfuie devant les Philistins.

sw.L: Yeye alikuwa pamoja na Daudi huko Pas-damimu, Wafilisti walipokuwa wamekusanyika huko kwa vita, na palikuwa na kipande cha shamba kilichojaa shayiri; na watu wakakimbia mbele ya Wafilisti.
sw.B: Yeye alikuwa pamoja na Daudi huko Pas-damimu wakati Wafilisti walipokuwa wamekusanyika huko kwa vita. Palikuwa na kipande cha shamba kilichojaa shayiri, na askari wakawakimbia Wafilisti.
sw.R: Yeye alikuwa pamoja na Daudi huko Pas-damimu, mahali Wafilisti walipokuwa wamekusanyika kwa vita. Palikuwa na shamba lililojaa shayiri, na jeshi la Israeli likawakimbia Wafilisti.

vi.L: Ông ở với Đa-vít tại Pát Đa-mim khi người Phi-li-tin tập hợp ở đó để giao chiến; ở đó có một thửa ruộng đầy lúa mạch, và dân chúng chạy trốn trước mặt người Phi-li-tin.
vi.B: Ông ở với Đa-vít tại Pát Đa-mim khi quân Phi-li-tin tập hợp ở đó để giao chiến. Ở đó có một thửa ruộng đầy lúa mạch, và quân lính chạy trốn trước mặt quân Phi-li-tin.
vi.R: Ông ở với Đa-vít tại Pát Đa-mim, nơi quân Phi-li-tin đã tập hợp để giao chiến. Ở đó có một thửa ruộng đầy lúa mạch, và quân Y-sơ-ra-ên bỏ chạy trước mặt quân Phi-li-tin.

ko.L: 그는 바스담밈에서 다윗과 함께 있었는데, 그때 블레셋 사람들이 싸우려고 그곳에 모여 있었다. 그리고 보리가 가득한 밭이 있었는데, 백성은 블레셋 사람들 앞에서 도망쳤다.
ko.B: 블레셋 사람들이 싸우려고 바스담밈에 모였을 때, 그는 거기서 다윗과 함께 있었다. 그곳에는 보리가 가득한 밭이 있었는데, 군사들은 블레셋 사람들 앞에서 달아났다.
ko.R: 그는 바스담밈에서 다윗과 함께 있었다. 블레셋 사람들이 싸우려고 그곳에 모여 있었다. 그곳에는 보리가 가득한 밭이 있었는데, 이스라엘 군대는 블레셋 사람들을 피해 달아났다.

pt.L: Ele estava com Davi em Pas-Damim, quando os filisteus se reuniram ali para a batalha; e havia um pedaço do campo cheio de cevada, e o povo fugiu diante dos filisteus.
pt.B: Ele estava com Davi em Pas-Damim quando os filisteus tinham se reunido ali para a batalha. Havia um terreno cheio de cevada, e as tropas fugiram dos filisteus.
pt.R: Ele estava com Davi em Pas-Damim, onde os filisteus tinham se reunido para a batalha. Ali havia um campo cheio de cevada, e o exército de Israel fugiu dos filisteus.

decisions.choice: in place of 2 Samuel 23:9-11: one story at Pas-dammim, in a field of barley, with Shammah missing
decisions.reason: In Samuel, Eleazar's fight (2 Samuel 23:9-10) and Shammah's stand in a field of lentils (23:11-12) are two separate deeds. Chronicles has one story: Eleazar is with David at Pas-dammim, and the field is full of barley, not lentils. Shammah son of Agee is not named, though he would be the third of the Three. A copyist's eye may have jumped from one "the Philistines gathered" to the next, leaving out the end of Eleazar's story and the start of Shammah's.

decisions.choice: Pas-dammim: the Ephes-dammim of 1 Samuel 17:1
decisions.reason: Pas-dammim is a shorter form of Ephes-dammim, where the Philistines camped when David fought Goliath (1 Samuel 17:1). 2 Samuel 23:9 has "when they taunted" in its place.

decisions.choice: a plot full of barley: a crop the Philistines had come to plunder
decisions.reason: Barley was the first grain to ripen in spring (Ruth 1:22). Raiders often came at harvest to take the crops (Judges 6:3-4), so the men were defending their people's food.

decisions.choice: the people (Literal); the troops (Balanced); the army of Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 23:11, "the people" here is Israel's army.

decisions.choice: el pueblo (L); la tropa (B); el ejército de Israel (R)
decisions.reason: "The people" meaning the army, as in Samuel and Kings: the ordinary word at Literal, a word for troops at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: "le peuple" (L); "la troupe" (B); "l’armée d’Israël" (R)
decisions.reason: "The people" meaning the army, as the Samuel terms note: the ordinary word at Literal, the army at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: watu (L); askari (B); jeshi la Israeli (R)
decisions.reason: As in Samuel, "the people" meaning the fighting men is "watu" at Literal and "askari", "jeshi" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: "dân chúng" (L); "quân lính" (B); "quân Y-sơ-ra-ên" (R)
decisions.reason: "The people" meaning the army, as the Vietnamese Samuel: the ordinary word at Literal, soldiers at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: "백성" (L); "군사들" (B); "이스라엘 군대" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel note's choice for "the people" meaning the army, and as 2 Samuel 23:11 in Korean.

decisions.choice: Pas-Damim; cevada; o povo (L), as tropas (B), o exército de Israel (R)
decisions.reason: "Pas-Damim" is written like "Efes-Damim" in 1 Samuel 17:1 in Portuguese, the same place (m2). The field and the flight keep 2 Samuel 23:11 in Portuguese, with "cevada" where Samuel has "lentilhas" (m1).

source.text: וַיִּֽתְיַצְּב֤וּ בְתוֹךְ־הַחֶלְקָה֙ וַיַּצִּיל֔וּהָ וַיַּכּ֖וּ אֶת־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיּ֥וֹשַׁע יְהוָ֖ה תְּשׁוּעָ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they took their stand in [the] middle of the plot and delivered it, and struck down [the] Philistines; and saved Yahweh [with] a salvation great.

en.L: And they took their stand in [the] middle of the plot and rescued it and struck down [the] Philistines; and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saved [them with] a great victory.
en.B: But they took their stand in the middle of the plot, defended it and struck down the Philistines, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saved them with a great victory.
en.R: But David and Eleazar stood in the middle of the field and kept the Philistines from taking it. They killed the Philistines, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rescued Israel with a great victory.

es.L: Y ellos se plantaron en medio de la parcela, y la defendieron, e hirieron a los filisteos; y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [los] salvó [con] una gran victoria.
es.B: Pero ellos se plantaron en medio de la parcela, la defendieron e hirieron a los filisteos, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los salvó con una gran victoria.
es.R: Pero David y Eleazar se quedaron en medio del campo y no dejaron que los filisteos lo tomaran. Mataron a los filisteos, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} salvó a Israel con una gran victoria.

fr.L: Et ils se postèrent au milieu de la parcelle, et la délivrèrent, et frappèrent les Philistins ; et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [les] sauva [par] une grande victoire.
fr.B: Mais ils se postèrent au milieu de la parcelle, la défendirent et frappèrent les Philistins, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les sauva par une grande victoire.
fr.R: Mais David et Éléazar se sont tenus au milieu du champ et ils ont empêché les Philistins de le prendre. Ils ont tué les Philistins, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a sauvé Israël par une grande victoire.

sw.L: Wakasimama katikati ya kipande hicho wakakiokoa, wakawapiga Wafilisti; na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaokoa [kwa] wokovu mkuu.
sw.B: Lakini wao wakasimama imara katikati ya shamba hilo, wakalilinda, wakawapiga Wafilisti, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawaokoa kwa ushindi mkuu.
sw.R: Lakini Daudi na Eleazari wakasimama katikati ya shamba hilo, wakawazuia Wafilisti wasilichukue. Wakawaua Wafilisti, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawaokoa Israeli kwa ushindi mkuu.

vi.L: Họ đứng giữa thửa ruộng, giải cứu nó và đánh giết người Phi-li-tin; và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giải cứu [họ bằng] một chiến thắng lớn.
vi.B: Nhưng họ đứng vững giữa thửa ruộng, bảo vệ nó và đánh giết quân Phi-li-tin, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã giải cứu họ bằng một chiến thắng lớn.
vi.R: Nhưng Đa-vít và Ê-lê-a-xa đứng giữa thửa ruộng và không để quân Phi-li-tin chiếm lấy nó. Họ giết quân Phi-li-tin, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã giải cứu Y-sơ-ra-ên bằng một chiến thắng lớn.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 그 밭 한가운데 버티고 서서 그것을 지키고 블레셋 사람들을 쳤다. 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 큰 구원으로 구원하셨다.
ko.B: 그러나 그들은 그 밭 한가운데 버티고 서서 밭을 지켜 내고 블레셋 사람들을 쳐 죽였다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 큰 승리로 그들을 구원하셨다.
ko.R: 그러나 다윗과 엘르아살은 밭 한가운데 서서 블레셋 사람들이 그 밭을 빼앗지 못하게 했다. 그들은 블레셋 사람들을 죽였고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 큰 승리를 주셔서 이스라엘을 구하셨다.

pt.L: E eles se colocaram no meio do terreno, e o livraram, e feriram os filisteus; e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} [os] salvou [com] uma grande vitória.
pt.B: Mas eles se firmaram no meio do terreno, o defenderam e mataram os filisteus, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} os salvou com uma grande vitória.
pt.R: Mas Davi e Eleazar ficaram no meio do campo e não deixaram os filisteus tomá-lo. Eles mataram os filisteus, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} salvou Israel com uma grande vitória.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 23:12, with the verbs in the plural and "Yahweh saved with a great victory"
decisions.reason: In 2 Samuel 23:12 the verbs are singular, for Shammah alone. Chronicles has the plural, since David and Eleazar are both in the field (verse 13). Samuel says Yahweh "worked a great victory"; Chronicles says Yahweh "saved", using the verb that belongs with the noun for victory or salvation.

decisions.choice: they: David and Eleazar
decisions.reason: Verse 13 places Eleazar with David at Pas-dammim, so the plural verbs refer to the two of them, standing together when the army fled.

decisions.choice: Yahweh saved with a great victory: the victory is God's, though the men fought
decisions.reason: The noun means rescue or deliverance, here won in battle. The narrator credits it to Yahweh, as in 2 Samuel 23:10, 12 and 1 Samuel 14:6.

decisions.choice: saved them (Balanced); rescued Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb has no object in the Hebrew. Balanced and Readable supply the people saved, and Readable names David and Eleazar as m2 explains.

decisions.choice: akaokoa [kwa] wokovu mkuu
decisions.reason: Chronicles has the verb "save" with its own noun ("saved with a great salvation"), where 2 Samuel 23:12 has "worked a great victory"; Literal keeps the pair of related words, and Balanced and Readable say "akawaokoa kwa ushindi mkuu".

decisions.choice: "큰 구원으로 구원하셨다"
decisions.reason: Chronicles has the verb "saved" with its noun, where 2 Samuel 23:12 has "worked a great victory"; Literal keeps the repeated root, Balanced and Readable say "victory".

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 23:12 in the plural; salvou ... com uma grande vitória
